plate_findings.evidence: Caption identifies periostosis; the radiograph shows periosteal new bone formation along the tibia (arrow).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Clinical photograph of a patient with thickened furrowed scalp skin characteristic of cutis verticis gyrata in PHO. [raw subtype: primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy] B: Dorsal view of both hands showing bulbous enlargement of the distal digits consistent with digital clubbing, a classic PHO manifestation. [raw subtype: primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy] C: Radiograph of the lower leg demonstrates linear periosteal new bone formation along the tibial shaft, characteristic of PHO-associated periostosis. [raw subtype: primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy] D: The caption explicitly attributes the visible knee and ankle articular manifestations to PHO. The appearance is compatible with enlarged, prominent joints, although this finding is not in the allowed vocabulary. [raw subtype: primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy]

in_text_mentions: Digital clubbing, pachydermia and periostosis are considered the most common triad of PHO ( Figure 3 ). Clubbing, first described by Hippocrates over 2500 years ago, is characterized by painless enlargement at the distal parts of the extremities, affecting the daily use and appearance of the fingers. It occurs in almost all PHO patients, usually as the initial symptom, and sometimes may be the only manifestation.
